task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the claim that cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones be tested with n=24 units?
How should cut-heavy and drive-heavy play types be defined and shown to be reliable from play-by-play?
What sample size and power are needed to compare role reproduction between shaper groups?
How should role transfer be operationalised without outcome-derived labels or lookahead from partial 2025-26 data?

historical_evidence.finding: In 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether connector function reproduced after a move (rho +0.265, LOO AUC 0.622, permutation p=0.005; holds when dropping Gafford). [prior work] calls this exploratory, notes that almost all other pre-move predictors were null, and says the paper treats cut share as a boundary condition applying to connector portability predictions.

Matching a mover's initiation diet to a destination's thin jobs was tested on 198 movers, of whom 19 were taxonomy connectors; the 15.7% match rate left 5 matched connectors. The connector delta comparison was p=0.156 (n=5/14). The all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not hold as a continuous Spearman (-0.034).

DRIVE-as-BEST counters were tested against a feasibility-constrained play-type mix on 44 triggers from 13 teams. The observed gap (-0.066) was below the minimum detectable effect of 0.180 PPP at 80% power (SD about 0.34), so a null and an effect up to 0.18 PPP could not be distinguished.

An archived check of whether mover portability relates to destination net-rating change was recorded as underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality. No numbers were kept, and it was dropped from Paper 1.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector-specific diet-matching test of post-move outcomes, and the all-movers binary test of the same idea
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as limited by small sample: only 5 matched connectors. The all-movers binary p=0.0283 did not replicate as a continuous Spearman (-0.034), so it was not the licensed connector test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Test of DRIVE-as-BEST counters against a constrained play-type mix
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as low power with a large minimum detectable effect (0.180 PPP at n=44). The observed gap of -0.066 could not separate a true null from effects up to 0.18 PPP.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Destination net-rating change check for portable movers
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality. [prior work] does not keep the numbers and says the test needed a landing-spot correction and more power.

evidence_establishes: Within a different study family (connector movers, n=92), a pre-move cut-share measure was associated with connector function reproducing after a move, with [prior work] itself labelling this exploratory.
Small-sample mover and play-type tests in this project's history have repeatedly ended as untestable or underpowered (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]).
Earlier work in this project has been unable to resolve effects of roughly the size relevant here at samples of 44 or fewer, or at 5 matched connectors.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shapers specifically have more portable roles. SF-[prior work] studied connectors, not shapers, and used a different sample.
Any effect size or direction for the shaper question in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data.
Whether the cut-share boundary condition in SF-[prior work] replicates. [prior work] treats it as exploratory.
Whether role reproduction can be measured reliably from the present per-game files.
Whether a shaper-specific test is feasible with n=24 units.
own_inferences: With n=24 units, a correlation test at 80% power and alpha 0.05 (two-sided) can only detect |r| of roughly 0.55 or more. The effect in SF-[prior work] (rho about 0.27-0.31) would need roughly 80-120 units.
Comparing two groups of about 12 shapers each gives even less power for a moderate difference, and the group split is likely to be unstable.

The question as posed is a comparison of transfer rates between shaper types, but the units, the transfer criterion and the time window are not specified in the task. Those choices could change the answer.
uncertainties: The meaning of 'unit' in n=24 is not stated. It could be player, player-season or team-context.
The transfer criterion is undefined. Role reproduction after a move or across seasons needs a measure that does not use the outcome being predicted.
Cut and drive shares may be unreliable at low possession counts, and their reliability is unknown here.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13 and the 2025-26 playoffs only from 2026-06-21. Using partial data would create look-ahead and drift problems.
SF-[prior work] gives no numbers, so its evidence can only be read as a directional warning.
The retrieved records relate to different samples and definitions, so they inform the risks more than the expected effect size.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that similar questions in this project, at comparable or smaller samples, ended untestable or underpowered (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]). SF-[prior work] supplies the only positive signal, but it applies to connectors at n=92 and is exploratory. Together these changed the decision from a possible confirmatory test toward do_not_proceed as a confirmatory study with n=24, while leaving room for a descriptive pilot that defines the measures.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 units gives power only for correlations around |r|>=0.55. The effect size in the closest precedent (SF-[prior work], rho about 0.27-0.31) needs roughly 80-120 units, and a two-group comparison of shapers needs more.
Cut-share and drive-share classification from play-type records has not been shown to be reliable at the possession counts available per shaper.
Role reproduction after a move would be defined from later outcomes, so the transfer label and the predictor could be coupled unless defined independently.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study tested cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers' role transfer. SF-[prior work] is the closest precedent. It is exploratory, concerns connectors, and used n=92 movers. The other three records are underpowered or untestable tests of related mover and play-type questions. None substantially answers the shaper question.

risks.text: n=24 units is far below the sample needed to detect the effect size seen in the closest precedent. Null results would be uninformative.
Cut and drive shares, and any role-reproduction score, need reliability checks (split-half or cross-season stability) before use.
If transfer is measured by post-move function, the predictor and outcome may share definitions, inflating apparent association.
Selecting shapers with extreme cut or drive shares, or with extreme early performance, can produce regression to the mean in later role measures.
Team context, minutes, lineup quality, teammate creation and destination system could all drive both cut share and role reproduction.
Partial 2025-26 regular-season and playoff data (before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21) must not enter the features or labels.
Play-type frequencies and offensive systems change across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons, so pooled transfer comparisons may reflect era effects.
Testing cut and drive shares together with several roles, outcomes and transfer windows would inflate false positives, as seen in the exploratory SF-[prior work] analysis.
A placebo or permutation check is needed to show the association is not an artefact of the small sample.
Play-type labels from the NBA stats play-by-play and the derived graph records may misclassify cuts and drives.

design.estimand: Difference in the rate at which shaper role reproduces after a move or across seasons, comparing cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, or the rank correlation between pre-transfer cut share and transfer score. The confirmatory estimand should be fixed in advance.
design.unit: Not defined by the task. Proposed unit: player-transfer event (player-season pairs with a context change), with team context as a covariate.
design.sample: With n=24 units the study does not meet power. A confirmatory study needs roughly 90-120 eligible transfer events (the sample size implied by the SF-[prior work] effect), built from 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoff data only. Partial 2025-26 data is excluded. The minimum viable step with the current sample is a descriptive pilot that reports reliability and distributions, not a hypothesis test.
design.power: Use the sample-size calculation for correlation or group comparison at 80% power and alpha 0.05, with the effect size set from SF-[prior work] (rho about 0.27) rather than from a larger value. At n=24 the design has power only for |r|>=0.55, so it is underpowered for the effect that the closest precedent reports.
design.controls: Adjust for minutes and possession counts, team offensive system, teammate creation share, starter status and season. Use lineup-quality or landing-spot correction, as SF-[prior work] recommends. Measure cut and drive shares from separate split-half samples and report reliability.
design.falsification: Test drive-share prediction and shuffled-label placebo. Use a fixed transfer window set in advance. Check that the cut-share association does not appear for non-transfer player-seasons. The claim would be refuted if the cut-share association is not better than the drive-share association and the placebo.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary contrast (cut versus drive transfer). Treat other roles, windows and outcomes as exploratory with correction for multiple comparisons, such as Holm.
design.decision_rule: Support the claim only if the pre-registered primary contrast is significant at alpha 0.05 after correction, the effect exceeds the minimum detectable effect at the achieved sample, the association holds when the largest-influence units are removed, and the placebo fails to reproduce it. Otherwise report as inconclusive, or as a null only if the study is adequately powered.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, frozen before analysis. Exclude 2025-26 regular season before 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs before 2026-06-21, and document the data-version hash.
